item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Os contratos futuros de açúcar bruto na bolsa ICE subiram nesta segunda-feira, recuperando-se após atingirem a menor cotação em três semanas e meia no início do pregão, enquanto o cacau se recuperou de uma mínima de quase seis semanas. AÇÚCAR * O açúcar bruto fechou em alta de 0,12 centavo, ou 0,7%, a 17,48 centavos por libra-peso, após atingir uma mínima de três semanas e meia, de 17,26 centavos. * O açúcar bruto atingiu uma máxima de 15 meses no início deste mês, mas, desde então, vem sofrendo pressão devido à realização de lucros por parte de investidores que aguardam os resultados dos danos climáticos associados ao El Niño, segundo corretores. * Por outro lado, o açúcar continua sendo sustentado pela menor produção de beterraba na Europa, pelas perspectivas de redução da produção na Ásia para 2026/27 devido à falta de chuvas e pela menor produção no Brasil, principal produtor, em razão do excesso de chuvas. * A produção de cana-de-açúcar na Indonésia deve cair cerca de 25% este ano devido às condições de seca e aos incêndios florestais. * O preço do açúcar branco caiu 0,3%, para US$507,50 por tonelada métrica. CACAU * O cacau em Londres fechou em alta de £27, ou 0,7%, a £3.961 por tonelada, após atingir uma mínima de quase seis semanas de £ 4.036. * As chegadas de cacau aos portos da Costa do Marfim, principal produtor, totalizaram 16.000 toneladas métricas na semana encerrada em 20 de setembro, para um total de 20.500 toneladas desde o início da safra 2026/27. * "A oferta confortável no curto prazo continuou a pesar sobre o mercado. Os estoques (de cacau) monitorados pela bolsa permanecem relativamente abundantes, enquanto a recuperação da demanda tem sido lenta, já que os fabricantes continuam se esforçando para reduzir o uso de cacau", afirmou o ING em uma nota. * Acrescentou, no entanto, que o cacau continua apoiado por um déficit de oferta previsto para 2026/27. * A precipitação ficou abaixo da média na semana passada na maioria das principais regiões produtoras de cacau da Costa do Marfim, e os agricultores afirmaram que as condições de seca poderiam ameaçar o desenvolvimento da safra principal, que vai de setembro a fevereiro. * O contrato de cacau da Bolsa de Nova York subiu 0,5%, para US$5.351 por tonelada. CAFÉ * O café arábica fechou em baixa de 4,1 centavos, ou 1,5%, a US$2,764 por libra-peso, após atingir uma mínima de três meses de US$2,7425. * O café está sob pressão geral devido ao aumento nos estoques de arábica na ICE, ao crescimento das exportações do Brasil, principal produtor, e às condições climáticas favoráveis no Brasil e no Vietnã. * Os cafeeiros no Brasil estão florescendo mais cedo, levando analistas a prever que a safra de 2027 também possa amadurecer mais cedo e antecipar o aumento da oferta global. * O café robusta caiu 1,7%, para US$3.337 a tonelada. O mercado atingiu, mais cedo, uma mínima de mais de três meses, a US$ 3.307. (Reportagem de May Angel e Marcelo Teixeira) ((Tradução Redação São Paulo 55 11 56447751)) REUTERS RS

item.title: Canada sees scope for France LNG partnership, minister says
item.description: Canada could pursue an energy partnership with France involving liquefied natural gas from its Pacific coast, Canadian Foreign Minister Anita Anand said on Monday, a day after leaders of the two countries met and discussed energy cooperation.
item.dc:creator: John Irish
item.content:encoded: Canada could pursue an energy partnership with France involving liquefied natural gas from its Pacific coast, Canadian Foreign Minister Anita Anand said on Monday, a day after leaders of the two countries met and discussed [USN:L8N45A14H TEXT:"energy cooperation"]. Anand said it was "quite conceivable" for Canada to execute an energy partnership with a European country using LNG exported from Canada's west coast. "That goes for France," she said in an interview on the sidelines of the annual gathering of world leaders at the United Nations. French President Emmanuel [USN:L8N45A14H TEXT:"Macron"] has repeatedly called in recent days for deeper energy cooperation with Canada as Europe seeks to diversify supplies amid disruptions linked to the conflict in the Middle East and rising energy prices. Canada, the world's fifth-largest natural gas producer, shipped its first-ever liquefied natural gas export cargo in June from the recently constructed LNG Canada facility in British Columbia, which is led by Shell (SHEL.L) and is the first North American LNG export site with direct access to the Pacific Ocean. Anand said discussions on energy partnerships were taking place with countries around the world across a range of sectors including LNG, clean energy, wind, solar and nuclear power. "Every country I speak with asks about potential partnerships in energy," she said. Anand pointed to discussions earlier this year between [USN:L6N3UJ0RK TEXT:"Canada and Germany"] involving LNG supplies destined for Asia through a swap arrangement, under which Germany benefits from third-party sales rather than direct shipments. "There is a host of potential deals and relationships that we can execute on energy," she said, adding that Canada was looking to match its energy expertise with the needs of partner countries. German state-controlled energy group Uniper (UN0k.DE) at the end of July also finalised a 20-year liquefied natural gas purchase deal with Canada. Asked about prospects for cooperation with France, Anand said the same logic applied. Anand said energy would be among the topics discussed when she hosts Germany's foreign minister in Canada later this week, alongside critical minerals and artificial intelligence. She said Ottawa was seeking to deepen ties not only with the European Union as a bloc but also with individual member states. "What Canada is doing is deepening its relationship not simply with the EU as a whole, but with individual countries within the EU to ensure that our domestic population benefits," she said.

item.title: Canada aims to cut time needed for project reviews, and address strikes
item.description: Canada on Monday unveiled draft legislation that would speed up the approval process for major natural resource projects, a goal Prime Minister Mark Carney says is necessary to help deal with US tariffs.
item.dc:creator: David Ljunggren, Amanda Stephenson
item.content:encoded: Canada on Monday unveiled draft legislation that would speed up the approval process for major natural resource projects, a goal Prime Minister Mark Carney says is necessary to help deal with US tariffs. The bill would also make it more complicated for a labor minister to order striking workers in major industries back to work. Ottawa stepped in several times in 2024 and 2025 to settle work stoppages in crucial sectors, prompting union anger. Carney has said Canada has to cut back on obstacles to growth, in particular streamlining a complex federal approval process for infrastructure projects. Lengthy permitting times are one reason why some energy and resource projects in Canada have taken a decade or more to move from proposal to completion. ONE-YEAR APPROVAL TARGET The new bill will establish a one-year time frame for federal reviews and decisions, in part by conducting federal permit processes and reviews simultaneously instead of one after another. The bill sends a signal to the federal bureaucracy that it must become more efficient, said federal Natural Resources Minister Tim Hodgson in an interview, adding the civil service will be held accountable to the new one-year time frame. "What this is doing is signaling to every part of government that we need to raise our competence. We need to do our environmental work better and faster," Hodgson said. The government stressed that achieving the one-year timeline was not wholly dependent on the regulatory process, but would also require project proponents to provide data and project information in a timely manner. The new bill does not change the right of Indigenous groups in Canada to be consulted and accommodated on projects that are taking place on their territory, but Hodgson said those consultations need to be done better and faster. Carney's ruling Liberals have a majority in the House of Commons elected chamber, ensuring the legislation should eventually pass. Opposition parties could demand changes and drag out the approval process. LABOUR CODE CHANGES The bill also aims to address an article in the Labour Code allowing the jobs minister to quickly end strikes and lockouts to "maintain or secure industrial peace". Ottawa has invoked this article to end disputes in crucial sectors like railways, ports, airlines and postal services, to the outrage of unions. Ottawa now says that in major disputes, a special mediator would have to work with the parties for 21 days. The minister could not intervene before then hearing a report from the mediator as well as receiving an assessment from the federal employment ministry as to the damage a stoppage could do.

item.title: Nasdaq tem fechamento recorde, conforme volta otimismo sobre IA e rendimentos dos títulos do Tesouro recuam
item.description: O Nasdaq atingiu um recorde de fechamento na segunda-feira, impulsionado pelas valorizações da Advanced Micro Devices e de outras grandes empresas do setor de inteligência artificial, enquanto os rendimentos dos títulos do Tesouro recuaram em relação às máximas recentes e os preços do petróleo bruto caíram para a menor cotação em 11 dias, em meio a especulações sobre um possível avanço nas negociações sobre o Oriente Médio em uma reunião da ONU nesta semana.
item.dc:creator: Noel Randewich, Johann Cherian
item.content:encoded: O Nasdaq atingiu um recorde de fechamento na segunda-feira, impulsionado pelas valorizações da Advanced Micro Devices e de outras grandes empresas do setor de inteligência artificial, enquanto os rendimentos dos títulos do Tesouro recuaram em relação às máximas recentes e os preços do petróleo bruto caíram para a menor cotação em 11 dias, em meio a especulações sobre um possível avanço nas negociações sobre o Oriente Médio em uma reunião da ONU nesta semana. As ações do setor de chips registraram alta, com a Intel (INTC.O) saltando 12,2% e a Arm Holdings disparando 17%. O índice de chips PHLX (.SOX) subiu 4,3%. A Advanced Micro Devices (AMD.O) subiu cerca de 10%, atingindo pela primeira vez uma capitalização de mercado de US$ 1 trilhão. O Nasdaq registrou seu primeiro fechamento recorde desde 2 de junho, enquanto o S&P 500 encerrou cerca de 0,4% abaixo de seu fechamento recorde de 13 de agosto. Os investidores apontaram sinais que sugerem que os gastos com IA continuam em expansão, apesar dos recentes alertas de segurança emitidos pelos líderes das gigantes da IA há uma semana, que provocaram uma onda global de vendas no setor de tecnologia. O rendimento de referência dos títulos de 10 anos dos EUA caiu abaixo do nível psicologicamente importante de 5%, enquanto os futuros do petróleo Brent caíram abaixo de US$100 o barril, atingindo seu nível mais baixo desde 9 de setembro, para depois fechar em US$100,34 o barril. Enquanto Washington e Teerã trocavam ameaças ao longo do fim de semana, o presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, afirmou que estaria aberto a se reunir com o presidente iraniano, Masoud Pezeshkian, que deve participar da Assembleia Geral da ONU em Nova York nesta semana. “Fomos, de certa forma, condicionados a acompanhar o preço do petróleo e o rendimento dos títulos de 10 anos dos EUA, e se você observar esses dois fatores hoje, eles passaram de fatores adversos para favoráveis para este mercado, pelo menos no curto prazo”, disse Art Hogan, estrategista-chefe de mercado da B. Riley Wealth. As ações da Meta (META.O) dispararam 11,4% depois que o Wells Fargo elevou seu preço-alvo para a plataforma de mídia social, após o recente lançamento de seu assistente de IA, o Muse. O S&P 500 subiu 1,49%, encerrando o pregão em 7.764,70 pontos. O Nasdaq teve alta de 2,26%, para 27.122,09 pontos, enquanto o Índice Dow Jones Industrial avançou 0,71%, para 52.048,83 pontos. Os investidores continuaram cautelosos em relação às perspectivas para as taxas de juros depois que o Federal Reserve elevou as taxas na semana passada pela primeira vez em três anos para combater a inflação. Os operadores veem 50% de chance de outro aumento no mês que vem, segundo o FedWatch da CME. Estão previstos comentários de pelo menos 10 formuladores de política monetária nesta semana. As ações de empresas com exposição à Groenlândia, listadas nos Estados Unidos, subiram após avanços nas negociações diplomáticas entre os Estados Unidos e a Dinamarca sobre o status da Groenlândia. A Greenland Mines (GRML.O) triplicou de valor, enquanto a Greenland Energy (GLND.O) mais que dobrou. Uma cúpula entre a China e os EUA na quinta-feira poderá abordar temas como a possível prorrogação da trégua comercial entre as duas superpotências, a guerra no Irã e a regulamentação da IA. Um relatório indicou que os EUA propuseram prorrogar a trégua comercial por seis meses, enquanto a China buscava uma prorrogação mais longa. O bitcoin , um importante indicador de tolerância ao risco, subiu mais de 6%, atingindo a maior alta em mais de sete meses, impulsionando a Coinbase (COIN.O) e a Strategy (MSTR.O) . A Paramount Skydance (PSKY.O) caiu quase 3% depois que uma fonte informou à Reuters que a empresa havia chegado a um acordo com a Califórnia e outros 11 Estados que moviam uma ação judicial para impedir sua fusão de US$110 bilhões com a Warner Bros Discovery (WBD.O) . Oito dos 11 índices setoriais do S&P 500 subiram, liderados pelo setor de serviços de comunicação (.SPLRCL) , com alta de 4,16%, seguido por um ganho de 2,4% no setor de tecnologia da informação (.SPLRCT) .

item.title: Foto de Lula preso segurando placa com número 171 é falsa
item.description: Uma imagem do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva preso segurando uma placa com o número 171 é falsa.
item.dc:creator: Reuters Fact Check
item.content:encoded: Uma imagem do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva preso segurando uma placa com o número 171 é falsa. Estes são os principais detalhes: A imagem , que circula no Facebook, no Instagram e no Threads, mostra o presidente de camiseta vermelha com uma placa de identificação onde se lê “Polícia Federal. Lula da Silva. 171.542. 1980”. A foto foi gerada por IA , segundo a ferramenta da OpenAI que detecta o uso de tecnologia da empresa em conteúdos criados com suas ferramentas. Lula de fato foi detido em 1980, na ditadura militar. No entanto, a foto de sua prisão é em preto e branco, e o político está com uma placa que diz “Dops. 80. Nº 12712”. Na época, o presidente era líder sindical e foi preso por encabeçar uma greve no ABC Paulista. O Departamento de Ordem Política e Social (Dops) de São Paulo, não a Polícia Federal (PF), foi responsável pela detenção de Lula. Os Dops eram órgãos estaduais de repressão a opositores da ditadura. A imagem gerada por IA faz referência ao artigo 171 do Código Penal , que define o crime de estelionato. Em 1980, Lula foi enquadrado na Lei de Segurança Nacional. Veredicto: Falso. A foto de Lula preso com uma placa “171” foi gerada por IA e não se parece com o registro verdadeiro da sua detenção em 1980. Este artigo foi produzido pela equipe da Reuters Fact Check. item.title: Lula diz que não aplicará reciprocidade enquanto estiver negociando com EUA
item.description: O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva disse nesta segunda-feira que não aplicará a lei de reciprocidade enquanto o Brasil estiver em negociações comerciais com os Estados Unidos, após a imposição de tarifas a produtos brasileiros pelo presidente norte-americano, Donald Trump.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva disse nesta segunda-feira que não aplicará a lei de reciprocidade enquanto o Brasil estiver em negociações comerciais com os Estados Unidos, após a imposição de tarifas a produtos brasileiros pelo presidente norte-americano, Donald Trump. "Nós estamos negociando, e de novo, enquanto ainda estamos na mesa de negociações, eu não tenho que aplicar a lei da reciprocidade. Eu tenho que ser mais paciente. Mas é importante você saber que se não há acordo, nós vamos ter que aplicar a lei da reciprocidade", disse o presidente em entrevista à CNN Internacional. Lula destacou o fato de ter falado com Trump recentemente e, depois da conversa, as negociações terem sido reabertas. A primeira reunião, virtual, entre o ministro do Desenvolvimento, Indústria e Comércio, Márcio Elias Rosa, e o representante de Comércio dos EUA, Jamieson Greer, ocorreu há cerca de três semanas e serviu para reabrir as conversas, mas o governo brasileiro não espera avanços pelo menos até depois das eleições. Lula foi perguntado se pretendia seguir o caminho do Canadá e entrar em uma guerra tarifária com os EUA, caso as negociações não avancem. O presidente negou, e disse que se for necessário terá que analisar com cuidado as medidas a serem tomadas dentro da lei da reciprocidade. "Eu não quero entrar em uma guerra de tarifas com os EUA e nem com qualquer outro país. O que eu quero é negociar e acredito em negociações", afirmou. IMPERADOR Em Nova York para a abertura das Assembleia Geral das Nações Unidas, Lula pode encontrar de novo com o presidente norte-americano nos corredores da ONU, apesar de não haver nenhuma negociação para uma conversa. Os dois mantêm um relacionamento pessoal, apesar do momento entre os governos não ser dos melhores. Na entrevista, Lula admitiu que teme interferências dos Estados Unidos na eleição brasileira, especialmente do secretário de Estado, Marco Rubio, mas que até agora são apenas suspeitas. Apesar de ter aberto um canal direto com Trump, Lula voltou a dizer que o norte-americano se comporta como "um imperador", mas afirmou que não está tentando "desafiar os EUA", como colocou a entrevistadora. "Não se trata de desafiar os EUA, se trata de dizer que todo país tem sua soberania, todo mundo cuida dos seus interesses e os EUA não podem impor regras a ninguém", disse.

item.title: Moldovan leaders say will seek parliament's ok to declare energy, water emergency
item.description: Moldova's pro-European leaders said on Monday that they were asking parliament to declare a state of emergency for energy and water supply in connection with dangerously low levels on the Dniester River it shares with Ukraine.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Tanas
item.content:encoded: Moldova's pro-European leaders said on Monday that they were asking parliament to declare a state of emergency for energy and water supply in connection with dangerously low levels on the Dniester River it shares with Ukraine. Prime Minister Vasile Tofan, writing on social media after a meeting of Moldova's Security Council, said the government would present the appeal to the chamber on Tuesday to give the administration the powers needed to tackle difficulties. He said giving the government a free hand to act was critical as Moldova secured much of its gas, oil and electricity from outside the country. "We can't afford to wait for a crisis to start looking for solutions. This will give the government the necessary tools to step in at the first sign of need—and only where it's truly necessary," Tofan wrote. "The government will be ready to provide the economy and citizens with water, electricity, and heat, and vulnerable households with the support they need." President Maia Sandu, who has spearheaded a drive for Moldova to join the European Union by 2030, had earlier chaired the Security Council meeting and said its members had recommended introducing emergency regulations quickly. "The share of renewable energy sources has increased, but we still don't have the necessary capacity to cover consumption during peak hours," she told a press conference. "However, we need to be ready for any changes and provide solutions, no matter what is going on outside the country." Moldova's government has been concerned with low levels on the Dniester for months. A joint meeting of Moldovan and Ukrainian experts last month [USN:L8N4480G5 TEXT:"reduced flows"] through the Dniester hydropower station in southern Ukraine to permit irrigation of crops in Moldova. The situation on the Dniester was further complicated last March by a Russian [USN:L1N40508X TEXT:"attack"] on the hydropower plant that triggered an oil spill and polluted water systems in Moldova.

item.title: Ibovespa fecha em alta com aval externo e nova pesquisa eleitoral
item.description: O Ibovespa fechou em alta nesta segunda-feira, ultrapassando os 187 mil pontos no melhor momento, em meio a um ambiente favorável a risco no mercado internacional, com alívio nos rendimentos dos títulos do Tesouro norte-americano e queda dos preços do petróleo.
item.dc:creator: Paula Arend Laier
item.content:encoded: O Ibovespa fechou em alta nesta segunda-feira, ultrapassando os 187 mil pontos no melhor momento, em meio a um ambiente favorável a risco no mercado internacional, com alívio nos rendimentos dos títulos do Tesouro norte-americano e queda dos preços do petróleo. Índice de referência do mercado acionário brasileiro, o Ibovespa (.BVSP) avançou 0,74%, a 186.595,60 pontos, com investidores também repercutindo nova pesquisa eleitoral. Na máxima do dia, chegou a 187.434,25 pontos. Na mínima, marcou 185.246,81 pontos. O volume financeiro no pregão somou R$27,79 bilhões. Nos Estados Unidos, o índice acionário S&P 500 (.SPX) encerrou com acréscimo de 1,49%, apoiado por ações de empresas ligadas à inteligência artificial, em sessão marcada pelo recuo nos preços do petróleo, o que apoiou a queda nos rendimentos do Treasuries, como título de 10 anos marcando 4,953% no final do dia, de 4,996% na sexta-feira. De acordo com o economista-chefe e sócio-fundador da Forum Investimentos, Bruno Perri, embora a cotação do petróleo siga em patamar elevado, o movimento de queda favorece uma melhora no humor externo, uma vez que apoia perspectivas mais positivas para a inflação e para a curva de juros, com reflexos no apetite a risco. Na cena eleitoral brasileira, nova [USN:S8N44200V TEXT:"pesquisa BTG/Nexus"] mostrou que o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) reduziu sua vantagem sobre o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) no primeiro turno da eleição presidencial de outubro e seguiu numericamente à frente no segundo turno por um ponto percentual, embora ambos permaneçam em empate técnico. Também está previsto para a sessão um novo levantamento Quaest sobre a disputa pelo Palácio do Planalto. A disputa acirrada indicada em pesquisas até o momento, com melhora principalmente no desempenho de Flávio, tem repercutido positivamente na bolsa, uma vez que alimenta apostas de mudança no poder em Brasília. De acordo com Perri, a possibilidade de vitória de Flávio endossa perspectivas fiscais melhores. Ainda no radar do dia, [USN:L6N45D0I7 TEXT:"pesquisa Focus"] mostrou que economistas consultados pelo Banco Central passaram a ver a Selic em 13,50% ao ano ao final de 2026, de 13,75% estimados na semana anterior, entre outros ajustes nas projeções para o crescimento da economia e para a inflação neste ano. Dados da B3 mostraram nova saída líquida de estrangeiros das ações brasileiras no último dia 17, reduzindo o saldo positivo acumulado em setembro para R$5,597 bilhões, de R$6,287 bilhões até o dia 16. DESTAQUES ITAÚ PN fechou em alta de 1,77%, com a maioria dos bancos do Ibovespa no azul. BTG PACTUAL UNIT avançou 3,42%, SANTANDER BRASIL UNIT subiu 1,53% e BRADESCO PN encerrou com acréscimo de 0,94%. A exceção foi BANCO DO BRASIL ON (BBAS3.SA) , que terminou com declínio de 0,91%, tendo no radar dados operacionais da BB Seguridade. Analistas do Bank of America também afirmaram que continuam seletivos sobre bancos na América Latina, acrescentando que, no Brasil, preferem Itaú, "dada sua rentabilidade, balanço sólido e execução de primeira linha", enquanto mantêm uma postura cautelosa em relação ao Banco do Brasil, "devido às pressões sobre a qualidade dos ativos". VALE ON (VALE3.SA) recuou 1,12%, em meio ao movimento modesto dos futuros do minério de ferro na China. No setor de mineração e siderurgia, CSN ON (CSNA3.SA) saltou 6,5% e foi o destaque positivo após duas quedas seguidas, sendo que apenas na sexta-feira o papel caiu 6,4%. USIMINAS PNA fechou com acréscimo de 0,14% e GERDAU PN (GGBR4.SA) avançou 0,71%. PETROBRAS PN caiu 1,03%, em mais um pregão de queda dos preços do petróleo no mercado internacional, onde o barril sob o contrato Brent fechou com declínio de 3,4%, a US$100,34, em meio a expectativa de avanços diplomáticos na crise com o Irã. No noticiário, a diretora de Engenharia, Tecnologia e Inovação da Petrobras, Renata Baruzzi, afirmou à Reuters que o petróleo descoberto no [USN:S0N4040AS TEXT:"poço de Morpho"], na bacia da Foz do Amazonas, é de "altíssima qualidade", talvez melhor que o do pré-sal. A campanha exploratória para poços adjacentes a Morpho deve começar no ano que vem. C&A ON (CEAB3.SA) avançou 6,6%, em pregão positivo para ações sensíveis a juros em meio ao alívio nas taxas dos DIs. O índice de consumo da B3 (.ICON) subiu 1,9%. BB SEGURIDADE ON (BBSE3.SA) caiu 2,55%. Analistas do Citi chamaram a atenção para dados da Susep mostrando que a companhia teve queda de 19% no lucro líquido em julho ante o mesmo período do ano passado, refletindo parcialmente resultados financeiros mais fracos da BrasilPrev, enquanto os prêmios no segmento rural caíram 40% ano a ano, sinalizando demanda mais fraca após o novo Plano Safra.

item.title: Report: Commanders QB Jayden Daniels (elbow) undergoes MRI
item.description: Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels had an MRI on his dislocated left elbow and is not expected to play next week against the Seattle Seahawks, NFL Network reported Monday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels had an MRI on his dislocated left elbow and is not expected to play next week against the Seattle Seahawks, NFL Network reported Monday. Daniels dislocated his elbow on the final play of the first half in Washington's 37-20 road loss to the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday. As the Commanders attempted to score a touchdown rather than settle for a field goal, Daniels was stepped on by left guard Chris Paul and tripped trying to backpedal. He put his left (non-throwing) arm on the turf and his arm buckled under his body weight as he threw an incomplete pass. Washington coach Dan Quinn confirmed postgame that Daniels suffered a dislocation, the same injury he suffered to the same arm in a game against the Seahawks last season. The MRI will determine if there is any ligament damage. Daniels ended up missing seven of Washington's last eight games following his elbow injury last season. Marcus Mariota finished out Sunday's game at quarterback for Washington and went 11-of-16 for 111 yards and a touchdown. Mariota is expected to start next week's home opener against the defending Super Bowl champions. -Field Level Media

item.title: Aprovação de Trump cai para 32%, menor nível de sua carreira, diz pesquisa Reuters/Ipsos
item.description: O índice de aprovação do presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, caiu para 32% -- o mais baixo de sua carreira política --, em meio a críticas de seus pares republicanos sobre sua maneira de lidar com o custo de vida e à impopular guerra contra o Irã, mostrou uma nova pesquisa da Reuters/Ipsos.
item.dc:creator: Jason Lange
item.content:encoded: O índice de aprovação do presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, caiu para 32% -- o mais baixo de sua carreira política --, em meio a críticas de seus pares republicanos sobre sua maneira de lidar com o custo de vida e à impopular guerra contra o Irã, mostrou uma nova pesquisa da Reuters/Ipsos. A pesquisa, concluída no domingo, foi realizada durante um período de quatro dias em que Trump expulsou três grandes veículos de comunicação da Casa Branca e sugeriu que o icônico Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts de Washington — batizado em homenagem ao presidente assassinado John F. Kennedy — poderia ser demolido caso o próprio nome de Trump não pudesse ser acrescentado a ele. A pesquisa revelou que os eleitores estão cada vez menos dispostos a apoiar os pares republicanos de Trump nas eleições de meio de mandato de 3 de novembro, que determinarão o controle do Congresso pelos próximos dois anos. A aprovação geral de Trump caiu em relação aos 35% registrados na pesquisa Reuters/Ipsos da semana passada, com o apoio entre seus próprios republicanos caindo de 82% para 73%. Trump voltou à Casa Branca em janeiro de 2025 com a promessa de conter a inflação e pôr fim às guerras no exterior. Em uma pesquisa Reuters/Ipsos realizada poucas horas após sua posse, ele registrou um índice de aprovação de 47%. Apenas 17% dos entrevistados na nova pesquisa aprovaram sua gestão em relação ao custo de vida, principal questão que, segundo os norte-americanos, determinará seu voto nas eleições de novembro. IRÃ COBRA SEU PREÇO A insatisfação entre os republicanos com relação ao tema vem crescendo desde que Trump iniciou a guerra contra o Irã, em fevereiro, o que levou a um aumento acentuado nos preços da gasolina e do diesel. Agora, pela primeira vez, a parcela de republicanos que desaprovam a forma como Trump lida com o custo de vida supera a fatia dos que a aprovam -- 51% contra 44%. O índice de aprovação de Trump é mais baixo do que qualquer outro registrado para seu antecessor democrata, Joe Biden, cujo mandato também foi marcado por uma inflação galopante e que acabou desistindo da tentativa de reeleição depois que um fraco desempenho no debate aumentou as preocupações com sua idade. O ponto mais baixo de Biden foi de 35%, atingido no final de outubro de 2024. Apenas 34% dos entrevistados na pesquisa mais recente aprovam os ataques ao Irã. O conflito privou o mundo de uma parcela significativa do petróleo e do gás produzidos no Oriente Médio e ameaça alimentar uma inflação mais alta nos EUA e em outros lugares, à medida que as empresas repassam os custos mais elevados dos combustíveis aos consumidores. Trump afirmou inicialmente que o conflito duraria algumas semanas e que o Irã precisava ser bombardeado para impedir que desenvolvesse armas nucleares. Já em setembro, o líder republicano prometeu que a guerra terminaria “imediatamente após” a eleição. Mas o Irã não tem dado sinais de recuo e, nas últimas semanas, Teerã e seus aliados ameaçaram causar novas perturbações nos mercados de petróleo. Oitenta e dois por cento dos entrevistados na pesquisa — incluindo nove em cada dez democratas e três quartos dos republicanos — afirmaram que o conflito provavelmente se estenderia por um “período prolongado”. A pesquisa Reuters/Ipsos mostrou que os eleitores registrados que participaram da pesquisa escolheram os democratas em vez dos republicanos — 43% contra 35% — quando questionados sobre como votariam nas eleições de meio de mandato. A diferença de 8 pontos foi a maior vantagem dos democratas nas pesquisas Reuters/Ipsos deste ano. Para os republicanos, perder o controle de qualquer uma das Casas do Congresso poderia complicar a agenda de Trump nos últimos dois anos de seu mandato. Os resultados da pesquisa sobre as intenções de voto para o Congresso oferecem uma visão geral de qual partido os norte-americanos em todo o país querem ver no comando do Congresso, embora os resultados não capturem todas as nuances das disputas Estado a Estado e distrito a distrito que determinam o controle do Senado e da Câmara dos Deputados. Trump continua popular entre os republicanos na questão da imigração — com 79% de seu partido apoiando-o —, mas apenas 36% dos norte-americanos em geral apoiam sua abordagem ao assunto e 55% a desaprovam. Alguns aliados republicanos no Congresso têm alertado que sua campanha agressiva para deportar pessoas que estão ilegalmente no país corre o risco de afastar eleitores cujas famílias imigraram recentemente para os Estados Unidos, como alguns hispânicos. O levantamento mostrou que 35% dos entrevistados aprovam a abordagem de Trump no combate ao crime, em comparação com 50% que desaprovam. A pesquisa da Reuters/Ipsos foi realizada online e reuniu 1.277 respostas de adultos norte-americanos em todo o país. Ela tem margem de erro de 3 pontos percentuais.

item.title: EU continues talks on renewal of Russia sanctions, diplomats say
item.description: European Union countries are continuing deliberations on a proposed deal what would lift sanctions on Russia-linked billionaires Alisher Usmanov and Mikhail Fridman but ensure thousands of other individuals and organisations remain sanctioned, diplomats said on Monday.

item.title: Zelenskiy and US spy chief Ratcliffe meet in Ireland, sources say
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy met US CIA chief John Ratcliffe at Shannon Airport in Ireland, two people familiar with the matter said.
item.dc:creator: Tom Balmforth, Jonathan Landay
item.content:encoded: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy met US CIA chief John Ratcliffe at Shannon Airport in Ireland, two people familiar with the matter said. The meeting took place on Monday, one of the sources said. The other source said the pair spoke informally while their planes were being refueled without specifying a date. Both sources, who requested anonymity to discuss sensitive matters, declined to disclose details of their conversation. The meeting happened as Zelenskiy was traveling to New York to take part in the annual gathering of world leaders at the United Nations. Ratcliffe was on his way back from meeting Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi, one source said. Ratcliffe's meeting with Zelenskiy comes less than a month since the CIA chief traveled to Moscow to meet with Russia's top intelligence officials. Neither Ratcliffe nor the CIA have publicly disclosed what was discussed in Moscow. One of the sources, who confirmed the Zelenskiy meeting to Reuters, said Ratcliffe had been in Moscow to discuss Ukraine, but they declined to elaborate. The New York Times reported last month that Ratcliffe used his trip to share his bleak assessment of the state of the Russian war against Ukraine and to urge the Russians to cut a deal before their position weakens.

item.title: A timeline of Trump administration moves to weaken endangered species protections
item.description: US President Donald Trump has scaled back regulations meant to protect endangered wildlife as part of a broader push to reduce permitting obstacles for energy, mining, agriculture and other development.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: US President Donald Trump has scaled back regulations meant to protect endangered wildlife as part of a broader push to reduce permitting obstacles for energy, mining, agriculture and other development. The 50-year-old Endangered Species Act is credited with helping to save the bald eagle, the US national bird, along with the California condor and numerous other animals and plants from extinction. Here is a timeline of actions the administration has taken in Trump's second term: April 16, 2025 The administration [USN:L1N3QU0SE TEXT:"proposes"] rescinding the ESA's regulatory definition of "harm," arguing that habitat modification should not qualify as a prohibited "take" of a protected species. In the ESA, "take" is defined as "to harass, harm, pursue, hunt, shoot, wound, kill, trap, capture, or collect, or to attempt to engage in any such conduct." Environmental groups say the proposal could make it easier for developers to damage wildlife habitat. November 19, 2025 The Interior Department [USN:L1N3WV0TC TEXT:"proposes"] four rules to roll back former President Joe Biden's endangered species regulations. The proposals would make it easier to exclude areas from critical habitat designations by considering economic and national security impacts. March 31, 2026 The Endangered Species Committee unanimously [USN:L1N40I110 TEXT:"exempts"] Gulf of Mexico oil and gas operations from certain requirements of the Endangered Species Act, citing national security and domestic energy needs. It is the first ESA exemption approved in more than three decades. July 10, 2026 The administration [USN:L1N43C0OX TEXT:"finalizes"] a rule removing habitat destruction from the regulatory definition of "harm" under the ESA. The change allows habitat modification so long as protected animals are not directly injured or killed. Days later, environmental groups [USN:L6N43G1BL TEXT:"sue"] to block the rule. July 17, 2026 The administration finalizes additional ESA regulatory changes, ending automatic protections for newly listed threatened species and making it easier for regulators to consider economic and national security concerns when designating critical habitat. September 4, 2026 Trump signs an executive order directing the Interior Department to determine whether gray wolves and Mexican wolves qualify for delisting or downlisting under the ESA and, if so, begin that process. September 9, 2026 Twenty states and Washington, D.C., sue the administration, challenging the revised definition of "harm" and other ESA rule changes that they say unlawfully weaken protections for endangered and threatened species. September 14, 2026 An internal memorandum from US Fish and Wildlife Service Director Brian Nesvik instructs agency officials to adopt a narrower interpretation of the ESA's prohibition on "take" following repeal of the harm rule. The memo says a prohibited take occurs only when intentionally directed at a particular animal, potentially limiting enforcement. The Interior Department did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

item.title: Rams WR Puka Nacua (hip/groin) out vs. Giants
item.description: Los Angeles Rams star wide receiver Puka Nacua will not play in Monday night's home opener against the New York Giants, with the team making him inactive for Monday Night Football.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Los Angeles Rams star wide receiver Puka Nacua will not play in Monday night's home opener against the New York Giants, with the team making him inactive for Monday Night Football. Nacua had not practiced since Friday with what is listed as a hip/groin injury. Rams head coach Sean McVay referenced a sore groin for Nacua coming out of practice on Thursday. Nacua reeled in five catches for 74 yards in the Rams' 27-7 loss to the San Francisco 49ers on Sept. 10 in Melbourne, Australia. The 25-year-old led the NFL with 129 receptions last season and racked up 1,715 receiving yards with 10 touchdowns in 16 games. Through his first three NFL seasons plus one game this year, Nacua has 318 catches for 4,265 yards and 19 TDs. The Rams will also be without wide receiver Jordan Whittington due to a quadriceps injury. Veteran Davante Adams is expected to lead the wide receiver unit for quarterback Matthew Stafford. The only other active receivers are Konata Mumpfield, Xavier Smith and Tutu Atwell. The Rams also rely heavily on their four tight ends, led by Colby Parkinson and Tyler Higbee. --Field Level Media

item.title: Infantino says he is open to talks over FIFA reform
item.description: FIFA President Gianni Infantino has proposed an independent review of the world soccer body's decision-making, in a move that could help him regain support after the withdrawal of a controversial private investment plan.
item.dc:creator: Julien Pretot
item.content:encoded: FIFA President Gianni Infantino has proposed an independent review of the world soccer body's decision-making, in a move that could help him regain support after the [USN:L1N43X04P TEXT:"withdrawal"] of a controversial private investment plan. "First, I will ask the Council whether it wishes to commission an independent external review of FIFA’s current governance framework for major strategic initiatives and recommend potential improvements," Infantino wrote to the FIFA Council and all 211 member association presidents in a letter seen by Reuters. He also said he would propose consultations with confederations, member associations and other stakeholders on strengthening FIFA's decision-making. The proposals would examine who has a say in major initiatives, including the respective roles of the president, Bureau, Council and Congress, and how to improve transparency and accountability. Infantino faced a fierce backlash over his proposal to sell a 20% stake in FIFA's commercial rights, including the World Cup, to private investors. The plan was abandoned in July after opposition and boycott threats, with UEFA, the Asian Football Confederation and CONCACAF subsequently calling for changes to FIFA's leadership. His opponents have been [USN:L6N4520VY TEXT:"struggling"] to find a candidate to challenge Infantino, who will be running for re-election in March in Rabat. Sources familiar with the discussions told Reuters this month that he still had enough votes to win, prompting opponents to focus on curbing his powers. Infantino said the abandoned plan had explored whether selling a minority stake in a FIFA-controlled commercial company could raise more money for football development. It would not have involved giving up control over sporting decisions, he said. But the proposal became public before it could be presented in full to the Council and member associations, according to Infantino. "I recognise that, without the full context, this caused concern and created the impression that decisions had already been taken. They had not," he wrote in the letter sent on Monday. "It remained a proposal, not a decision, and was always subject to the necessary approvals of the Council and the Member Associations. It has now been withdrawn and will not proceed." Infantino said he had heard differing ideas about who should decide major strategic questions. Some favoured requiring unanimous agreement in the Bureau, while others wanted such matters put directly to Congress and the member associations. "My role is not to pre-judge that discussion. Those who support a particular model should have the opportunity to set out their case clearly," he wrote. Suggestions received by the October 15 Council meeting could be discussed there, with later submissions also considered within a deadline yet to be specified. Any changes to FIFA's statutes would need Congress approval. Infantino also said member associations' positions on proposals or governance matters would not affect their treatment by FIFA, whose development and solidarity programmes would continue under existing rules. "No association’s treatment will depend on its position on any proposal or institutional matter," he wrote. "I remain fully committed to leading FIFA and confident in what we can achieve together."

item.title: Falcons to start Michael Penix Jr. at Green Bay on Thursday
item.description: Michael Penix Jr. will start at quarterback for the Atlanta Falcons on Thursday at Green Bay.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Michael Penix Jr. will start at quarterback for the Atlanta Falcons on Thursday at Green Bay. The team made the announcement Monday after Atlanta coach Kevin Stefanski initially kept the decision under wraps. Penix is making his first NFL start since he suffered a season-ending ACL tear Nov. 16, 2025 against the Carolina Panthers. It was the third time in his career Penix endured a torn ACL. The Falcons' first-round pick (eighth overall) in the 2024 NFL Draft, Penix has been practicing for three weeks. Last week, offensive coordinator Tommy Rees said Penix was excellent in practice but Atlanta (0-2) held him out for one more game. Tua Tagovailoa, who signed with Atlanta in the offseason, could also be available after he was inactive for the first two games of the season with an oblique injury suffered days before the team's season opener at the Pittsburgh Steelers. Cooper Rush started the first two games but neither outing went to script. He completed 56.4% of his passes for 229 yards, one touchdown and four interceptions before he was benched during Sunday's 34-3 home loss to the Panthers. Undrafted rookie Jack Strand replaced Rush against the Panthers, completing 8 of 15 passes for 59 yards and an interception -- which was returned for a touchdown -- in his regular-season debut. The Packers (1-1) are coming off an overtime win against the Jets in New Jersey. --Field Level Media

item.title: AI could boost LatAm, Caribbean economy 5.1% over a decade but wages may fall, IDB says
item.description: Adoption of artificial intelligence could leave economic output in Latin America and the Caribbean 5.1% higher after a decade, while its effect on wages will depend on whether workers can move into expanding jobs, according to forthcoming research from the Inter-American Development Bank.
item.dc:creator: Rodrigo Campos
item.content:encoded: Adoption of artificial intelligence could leave economic output in Latin America and the Caribbean 5.1% higher after a decade, while its effect on wages will depend on whether workers can move into expanding jobs, according to forthcoming research from the Inter-American Development Bank. The IDB’s 2026 flagship report, due in November, estimates that regional economic output could be only 0.3% higher under limited AI adoption and small productivity gains. Wages could increase by 2.3% to 5.3% if workers move into jobs in expanding sectors, but fall by 13.5% to 20.9% if they do not. The IDB is the largest development lender in Latin America and the Caribbean and has 48 member countries, including 26 borrowing members in the region. IDB President Ilan Goldfajn also called for more financing, long-term purchase contracts and minimum prices to support critical-minerals supply chains. He said minerals produced in ways that respect labor conditions and the environment should be differentiated from supply produced without those safeguards and referred to a minimum price for buyers as a “buyers’ club.” Goldfajn discussed AI and critical minerals with regional leaders, including the heads of state of Chile and Uruguay, as well as executives from Alphabet, Meta and Anthropic at a closed-door meeting on Monday. In an interview before that meeting, he gave no details on how the club or price mechanism would work, who might participate or whether the IDB would provide financial backing.

item.title: Nestle Russia pledges to continue operations despite Kremlin transfer of assets
item.description: Nestle's Russian subsidiary pledged to continue its operations in Russia without regard to a decision by the Kremlin to transfer control of the company's assets, the Swiss food giant was quoted as saying on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Nestle's (NESN.S) Russian subsidiary pledged to continue its operations in Russia without regard to a decision by the Kremlin to transfer control of the company's assets, the Swiss food giant was quoted as saying on Monday. "The Nestle Group in Russia is continuing its commercial activities in Russia in full and wishes to state its intention to unconditionally fulfil all obligations to clients, partners, and employees," state news agency TASS quoted the company's Russian press service as saying in a statement in Russian. The Russian assets of Nestle and French retailer Auchan were, by virtue of a presidential decree on Friday, [USN:L8N45A06P TEXT:"transferred"] to temporary control by L.E.V. Management, a little-known company with no public profile. The Nestle statement quoted by TASS said the transfer did not amount to nationalisation or a change of ownership. It said Nestle expressed confidence that working with the team at L.E.V. Management would help the company continue to grow and improve its efficiency. After the presidential decree was announced last week, Nestle, maker of Nescafe coffee and KitKat chocolate bars, said it was "committed to taking all necessary steps to protect its rights and ensure continuity of business operations in the interests of all stakeholders, particularly its employees". The Kremlin said hostile actions by "unfriendly" countries played a role in its decision to take control of the Russian assets of Nestle and Auchan. In previous cases, temporary administration has often been followed by state expropriation, with assets later transferred to Kremlin-linked individuals or companies. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said only temporary administration was under consideration for now.

item.title: Trump approval falls to record low of 32% as high costs bite, Reuters/Ipsos poll finds
item.description: President Donald Trump's approval rating fell to 32% - the lowest of his political career - as his fellow Republicans soured on his handling of the cost of living amid the unpopular Iran war, a new Reuters/Ipsos poll found.
item.dc:creator: Jason Lange
item.content:encoded: President Donald Trump's approval rating fell to 32% - the lowest of his political career - as his fellow Republicans soured on his handling of the cost of living amid the unpopular Iran war, a new [USN:L6N43U101 TEXT:"Reuters/Ipsos poll"] found. The poll, completed on Sunday, was conducted over a four-day period that saw Trump [USN:L1N45D0B5 TEXT:"throw three major news organizations out of the White House"] and muse that Washington's iconic Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts -- named after slain President John F. Kennedy -- could be [USN:L6N45A17H TEXT:"torn down"] if Trump's own name could not be added to it. It found voters leaning away from supporting Trump's fellow Republicans in the November 3 midterm elections that will determine control of Congress for the next two years. Trump's overall approval was down from a reading of 35% in last week's Reuters/Ipsos poll, with support among his own Republicans down to 73% from 82% a week earlier. Trump returned to the White House in January 2025 on promises to tame inflation and end foreign wars. In a Reuters/Ipsos poll conducted in the hours after he was sworn in, he enjoyed a 47% approval rating. Just 17% of respondents in the new poll approved of his handling of the cost of living - the top issue Americans say will determine how they vote in November. IRAN TAKES A TOLL Dissatisfaction among Republicans on inflation has been growing since Trump launched the war on Iran in February that has pushed gasoline and diesel prices sharply higher. Now for the first time, Republicans who disapprove of Trump's handling of the cost of living outnumber those who give him a thumbs up - 51% to 44%. Trump's approval rating is lower than any recorded for his Democratic predecessor, Joe Biden, whose presidency was also marked by surging inflation and who ultimately ended his reelection bid after a poor debate performance heightened concerns about his age. Biden's low was 35%, reached in late October 2024. Only 34% of the most recent poll respondents approve of the strikes on Iran. The conflict has cut the world off from a significant slice of the oil and gas produced in the Middle East, and threatens to stoke higher inflation in the US and elsewhere as businesses pass on higher fuel costs to consumers. Trump initially said the conflict would last a few weeks and that Iran needed to be bombed to stop it from developing nuclear weapons. Earlier this month, the Republican leader pledged the war would end "immediately after" the election. But Iran has shown no sign of giving up and in recent weeks Tehran and its allies have threatened further disruptions to oil markets. Some 82% of poll respondents - including nine in ten Democrats and three-quarters of Republicans - said the conflict would likely go on for an "extended period of time." The Reuters/Ipsos poll showed registered voters in the poll picked Democrats over Republicans - 43% to 35% - when asked how they would vote in the midterms. The 8-point gap was the biggest lead for Democrats in Reuters/Ipsos polling this year. For Republicans, losing control of either chamber could complicate Trump's agenda in the last two years of his term. The poll results on congressional voting plans provide an overall view of which party Americans nationwide want to see in charge in Congress, though the results don't capture all the nuances of the state-by-state and district-by-district contests that determine control of the Senate and House of Representatives. Trump remains popular among Republicans on the issue of immigration - with 79% of his party backing him - but only 36% of Americans overall support his approach to the matter and 55% disapprove. Some Republican allies in Congress have warned that his aggressive campaign to deport people in the country illegally risks alienating voters with family who recently immigrated to America, like some Hispanics. Some 35% of poll respondents approve of Trump's approach to fighting crime, compared to 50% who disapprove. The Reuters/Ipsos poll was conducted online and gathered 1,277 responses from US adults nationwide. It had a margin of error of 3 percentage points.

item.title: Miles de vuelos en EEUU se ven complicados por un problema de telecomunicaciones
item.description: Un fallo en un circuito de telecomunicaciones y la rotura de un cable de fibra óptica provocaron el lunes el caos en miles de vuelos en todo Estados Unidos y obligaron a suspender las llegadas a los principales aeropuertos de Nueva York, Boston y Filadelfia.
item.dc:creator: David Shepardson
item.content:encoded: Un fallo en un circuito de telecomunicaciones y la rotura de un cable de fibra óptica provocaron el lunes el caos en miles de vuelos en todo Estados Unidos y obligaron a suspender las llegadas a los principales aeropuertos de Nueva York, Boston y Filadelfia. Los vuelos se suspendieron el mismo día en que 130 líderes mundiales y decenas de ministros llegaban a Nueva York para la reunión anual de alto nivel de la Asamblea General de las Naciones Unidas. La Administración Federal de Aviación (FAA) suspendió el lunes el tráfico de llegada a los concurridos aeropuertos de la costa este Estados Unidos, y en un momento dado detuvo los vuelos en los tres principales aeropuertos del área de Nueva York, así como en los de Filadelfia y Boston y en dos más pequeños del área de Nueva York. FlightAware, una página web de seguimiento de vuelos, indicó que más de 5.600 vuelos en Estados Unidos sufrieron retrasos o fueron cancelados, incluidos 1.200 vuelos en los tres aeropuertos del área de Nueva York. El problema también obligó a desviar más de 100 vuelos a otros aeropuertos. El incidente puso de manifiesto la fragilidad del anticuado sistema de control del tráfico aéreo de Estados Unidos, al que el Congreso destinó el año pasado 12.500 millones de dólares para su modernización. El secretario de Transporte, Sean Duffy, explicó que un equipo de obras del sistema de ferrocarriles Amtrak cortó accidentalmente un cable de fibra óptica en Nueva Jersey, lo que provocó una interrupción de las comunicaciones y obligó a la FAA a suspender los vuelos en el noreste. El administrador de la FAA, Bryan Bedford, explicó que un circuito de sustitución había fallado en el Centro de Control de Aproximación por Radar de Filadelfia. La FAA no reactivará el sistema para los vuelos entrantes en los aeropuertos afectados "hasta que nos aseguremos de que el espacio aéreo es seguro", dijo Bedford. La pérdida de comunicaciones se debió a un fallo en un circuito de una instalación de control de tráfico aéreo de Filadelfia, que gestiona el tráfico aéreo de los aeropuertos, explicó Bedford. Posteriormente, las autoridades descubrieron que una línea de fibra óptica de reserva había sido cortada accidentalmente por un equipo de obras en Nueva Jersey. "Cuando se activó el sistema de respaldo, descubrimos que la fibra de respaldo tenía una rotura, y que la reparación de esa rotura probablemente llevará unas 13 horas. Me han dicho que es una avería de gran envergadura. Mientras tanto, ya tenemos listo el nuevo circuito para su instalación", dijo Bedford.

item.title: Venezuelan delegation in NY seeks debt, energy deals
item.description: A Venezuelan delegation led by interim President Delcy Rodriguez that is taking part in the United Nations General Assembly this week began discussing energy, debt and mining issues with counterparties in the US on Monday, officials and sources said.
item.dc:creator: Marianna Parraga, Vivian Sequera
item.content:encoded: A Venezuelan delegation led by interim President Delcy Rodriguez that is taking part in the United Nations General Assembly this week began discussing energy, debt and mining issues with counterparties in the US on Monday, officials and sources said. The talks are expected to lead to the signing of agreements as part of US President Donald Trump's plans to rebuild Venezuela's key industries, while removing obstacles for Rodriguez's government to regain control of assets overseas and have access to financing, according to the sources. In one of her first meetings, she held talks with Inter American Development Bank President Ilan Goldfajn. She later met International Monetary Fund Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva, and World Bank President Ajay Banga, in separate meetings, according to state TV and sources. "Her visit will have a big focus on debt restructuring, funds and payments," one of the sources said. Venezuela announced in May it would begin restructuring its sovereign debt and that of state oil company PDVSA, estimated by most analysts at between $150 billion and $200 billion. Last month, legal and financial advisers launched a [USN:L6N44N0R5 TEXT:"committee"] to bring together companies with outstanding claims against Venezuela ahead of the planned restructuring. The initiative aims to coordinate creditors' participation in the process and secure representation for them in negotiations. The IDB is drawing up a two-year engagement plan for Venezuela focused partly on electricity and social protection, Goldfajn told Reuters. The effort includes missions to examine the nation's macroeconomic framework and data and to estimate investment needs across different sectors. With the IMF, talks focused on earthquake recovery and reconstruction in Venezuela, Georgieva said on social media. The Venezuelan government and a faction of the opposition are separately nearing a [USN:FWN4590XP TEXT:"deal"] to move some $4 billion in gold from the Bank of England to the US, sources told Reuters earlier this month. Rodriguez arrived in New York early on Monday with her team. It was her first trip to the US after taking office as Venezuela's interim president in January under Washington's oversight, following the capture of then President Nicolas Maduro by US forces. The top US diplomat in Venezuela, John Barrett, received her at the airport, Venezuela's state TV said. Rodriguez met UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres late in the afternoon to discuss economic reforms, debt restructuring, dialogue initiatives, and cooperation between the UN and Venezuela, "including on human rights, as well as the path toward a full democracy," the UN said statement. DEMOCRACY, HUMAN RIGHTS Venezuela's Foreign Affairs Minister Felix Plasencia met UK officials to discuss democratic transition and human rights, as well as recovery efforts following this year's earthquakes, said Chris Elmore, UK minister for the Americas. Plasencia later had talks with US Assistant Secretary of State for Western Hemisphere Affairs, Juan Pablo Segura. "US companies can continue to power Venezuela's economic recovery, help restore investor confidence, and deliver jobs and energy dominance for the American people," Segura said on X. Venezuelan ministers and top officials advanced in negotiations for months ahead of Rodriguez's trip to New York, where she is scheduled to meet Trump on Tuesday. The planned meeting between Trump and Rodriguez — who was Venezuela's vice president under Maduro — will take place on the sidelines of a reception hosted by the US President, the US Ambassador to the United Nations, Mike Waltz, said during a recent press briefing call. Venezuela's Foreign Affairs and Information ministries did not immediately reply to requests for comment. Some Venezuela-owned buildings in New York that had been shut for years, including a consulate and the office of the country's UN mission, have recently been renovated for their reopening, according to media reports. The meeting between Rodriguez and IDB officials, where oil minister Paula Henao also was present, was at the UN mission's building. Henao, Mining Minister Hector Silva and top officials from PDVSA participated this month in a G20 energy conference in Houston, where [USN:S0N42Y01V TEXT:"a memorandum of understanding"] was inked with US oil producer Continental Resources for an area in Venezuela's main output region, the Orinoco Belt. A separate contract was also signed granting US investment firm Heeney Capital operational and export rights for a gold mine. Another [USN:L6N458178 TEXT:"preliminary agreement"] has been in negotiation for months with US energy major ExxonMobil , which could ultimately lead to its return to Venezuela's oilfields, sources said this month.

item.title: OpenAI calls for US to take lead in global efforts to develop technical standards
item.description: Artificial intelligence giant OpenAI called on Monday for the United States to lead an international effort to develop global technical standards for frontier AI, including recursive self-improvement, where systems can autonomously enhance their own capabilities.
item.dc:creator: Michelle Nichols
item.content:encoded: Artificial intelligence giant OpenAI called on Monday for the United States to lead an international effort to develop global technical standards for frontier AI , including recursive self-improvement, where systems can autonomously enhance their own capabilities. AI will be a key topic of discussion at the high-level UN General Assembly this week after several AI industry leaders — including OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman — called for a coordinated slowdown of the development of the [USN:L6N45A0PY TEXT:"increasingly powerful technology"], warning it could soon improve on its own and slip beyond human control. In a blog post published as world leaders gather at the United Nations, OpenAI said it was essential that a mechanism to facilitate complementary national and international frontier standards be developed, along with common measurements and incident reporting protocols for better collective action. "Leading now will determine whether the United States shapes the global AI framework or watches a fragmented, uneven, and conflict-ridden system take hold around it. This will also determine whether advanced AI strengthens the networks that the United States and its allies already have; failing to lead may weaken them," OpenAI wrote in Monday's blog post. Given worries about AI potentially harming humans in the future, the industry has been talking about intentionally slowing development, or "pacing". "Pacing AI development is not about maintaining a predetermined speed. Technically, it is about ensuring that alignment research and deployment of that research stay ahead of capabilities," OpenAI said. Alignment ensures AI acts in line with human values. UN SECURITY COUNCIL TO MEET [USN:L6N45A15J TEXT:"Altman is due to brief"] the 15-member UN Security Council on Wednesday on AI and international security. The meeting has been convened by France, which is the president of the body for September, and will be chaired by French Minister for Europe and Foreign Affairs Jean-Noël Barrot. The UN Security Council, which is charged with maintaining international peace and security, met for the first time on the risks of artificial intelligence in 2023, when China said the technology should not become a "runaway horse" and the United States warned against its use to censor or repress people. US President Donald Trump's administration has rejected calls to slow down AI development, wary that any pause would only hand China room to close the gap in a technology it views as central to national and economic security. Trump said earlier this month that the US already has guardrails in place to regulate AI development, adding that China would benefit from the doubt being cast on AI development. Trump is [USN:L8N45A068 TEXT:"scheduled to meet"] with Chinese President Xi Jinping this week in Washington.

item.title: Jarvis Cocker remembers Pulp's first time in new documentary
item.description: Almost half a century after their birth, Britpop darlings Pulp are stars of a documentary that delves back into the band's roots in the childhood dreams of gangly frontman Jarvis Cocker.
item.dc:creator: Shaurya Thapa
item.content:encoded: Almost half a century after their birth, Britpop darlings Pulp are stars of a documentary that delves back into the band's roots in the childhood dreams of gangly frontman Jarvis Cocker. In "Pulp: What Do You Do For An Encore?" Cocker narrates flashbacks based on diary entries he scrawled out at school in the northern English city of Sheffield in the 1970s, mapping out his "masterplan" for Pulp's success. "I was maybe 12 or 13 ... I couldn't play the guitar yet but I could write," Cocker told Reuters. "It was ... wish fulfilment. I suppose like manifesting." He got his friends to rehearse at his mother's house, bribing them by "buying some lager". The film, directed by "Son of Rambow"'s Garth Jennings, moves on to his time studying film and fine art in London — at the "St Martin's College" immortalised in their future hit "Common People". "I graduated but ... what really I felt a pull to do was to write songs," he added. "I think that's my way of trying to make sense of the world and out of myself." Pulp struggled to find success in the 1980s, then rose to mainstream success in the 1990s with albums such as "His 'N' Hers" and the Mercury Prize-winning "Different Class" and a string of other hits from "Do You Remember The First Time?" to "Disco 2000" to "Help the Aged". After a 24-year-long recording hiatus, they returned in 2025 with the Mercury Prize-nominated "More". The film captures the band’s performances from their reunion shows at London’s O2 Arena. As for the future, "I think I won't be alive ... in 24 years, or if I am, I won't be up to it," Cocker said. "But, we did an album. It went well ... Everybody is still talking to each other, so I would really hope that we will make something else. But I don't know how long that will take." "Pulp: What Do You Do For An Encore?" begins streaming on MUBI on September 25.

item.title: Thousands of US flights snarled before FAA resolves telecom problem
item.description: Thousands of flights across the US were snarled on Monday, with incoming flights halted for hours at major East Coast airports, before the Federal Aviation Administration resolved a telecommunications problem late in the afternoon.
item.dc:creator: David Shepardson
item.content:encoded: Thousands of flights across the US were snarled on Monday, with incoming flights halted for hours at major East Coast airports, before the Federal Aviation Administration resolved a telecommunications problem late in the afternoon. The issue started around 9:45 a.m. when workers accidentally cut a telecom line in New Jersey used by the FAA. This forced a halt to incoming flights at major airports on the day that 130 world leaders and dozens of ministers were arriving in New York for the annual high-level meeting of the United Nations General Assembly. The FAA stopped arrivals at all three major New York-area airports as well as Philadelphia and Boston and two smaller airports in the New York area. The problems were not fully resolved for eight hours. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy posted on X late in the afternoon that telecom lines had been repaired and normal operations throughout the Northeast were resuming. He said it would take time to resolve existing delays and urged passengers to check the status of flights they were waiting for. FlightAware, a flight-tracking website, said about 7,000 flights were delayed or canceled, including 1,400 flights at the three major New York-area airports. More than half of all flights were canceled at Newark, a major United Airlines (UAL.O) hub. United said it issued a travel waiver to help impacted passengers. The issue also forced the diversion of more than 100 flights to other airports. The incident demonstrated the fragility of the aging US air traffic control system, which Congress awarded $12.5 billion for upgrades last year. New Jersey Transit said a crew had been digging at one of its work sites 10 feet away from the utility markings and it was still trying to determine if Verizon or the contractor made the markings. Duffy initially blamed an Amtrak construction crew, which he said accidentally cut into a fiber line in New Jersey near New Brunswick, causing a telecom outage and forcing FAA to pause flights in the Northeast. Amtrak said it was not responsible. Around 5:30 p.m., New Jersey Transit said most of the fiber cables had been repaired and should be coming back online shortly. Newark Airport reopened for arriving flights after eight hours and LaGuardia also reopened after being shuttered for flights for much of the afternoon. Verizon said it was working to repair the damaged cable near the Amtrak rail line and to restore connectivity as quickly as possible. Flights at Philadelphia had again resumed late in the afternoon after a second ground stop was lifted. Reagan Washington National Airport also halted flights for more than an hour because of volume issues. FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford said a replacement circuit had failed at Philadelphia Terminal Radar Approach Control, which was the primary communications for the center. A ground stop at Boston, which stopped accepting flights because of spillover volume, was also lifted. “The timing is absolutely horrible and I’m very sorry for the delays and cancellations,” Bedford told reporters. He stressed that safety was the top priority. “We’re going to do what is necessary to make sure the airspace is safe.” The loss of communications was tied to a failed circuit at a Philadelphia air traffic control facility that handles air traffic for the airports, Bedford said. Then authorities discovered that the construction crew had accidentally cut a backup fiber line. "When it went to flip into the backup, we discovered that the backup fiber had a break, and that fiber break is probably 13 hours to repair. It's massive, I'm told. Meanwhile, we've got the new circuit ready to install now," Bedford said. Philadelphia is an American Airlines (AAL.O) hub. In May 2025, the Philadelphia facility that guides air traffic in and out of Newark airport suffered a series of significant communications outages. The FAA said last year a telecommunications outage impacted communications and radar displays at Philadelphia TRACON. Last year, Congress approved $12.5 billion to start upgrading the aging air traffic control system, and boost controller hiring following decades of complaints over airport congestion and flight delays and a series of technology issues in recent years. Duffy said Congress needed to approve another $17.5 billion to finish the job. "This is unacceptable in America," Duffy said.

item.title: China's GAC looks to add car production capacity in Europe
item.description: Guangzhou Automobile Group aims to add production capacity in Europe to bolster its planned large-scale roll-out of cars in major markets like France, GAC France's deputy chief executive, Cedric Lacour, said on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Guangzhou Automobile Group (601238.SS) aims to add production capacity in Europe to bolster its planned large-scale roll-out of cars in major markets like France, GAC France's deputy chief executive, Cedric Lacour, said on Monday. The Chinese auto maker's partner, Magna (MG.TO) , currently produces the vehicles sold in Europe, where GAC has also expanded to Finland, Greece, Poland, Portugal, Spain and the United Kingdom. "We are currently looking into production capacity in Europe, both with Magna and with other investors," Lacour told Reuters on the sidelines of an event in Paris where GAC unveiled the compact EVs Aion UT and Aion V, its first two cars for the French market. "We really want to establish a long-term presence here (in Europe), which automatically means we need production capacity," he said. GAC plans to have launched 12 electric and hybrid models in France by 2030, Lacour said during a presentation, adding the auto maker also plans to operate 50 dealerships in France this year, rising to 200 by 2030. "Our goal is to take a brand from launch to scaling up in just four years," he said. Asked if GAC, founded in 1997, was late and trailing some rivals in coming to Europe, Lacour said it was "entering the market at just the right time". In July and August, EVs reached record shares of new car registrations of 35% and 38% in France, boosted by higher fuel prices linked to the Iran war.

item.title: Lula diz que Uruguai cedeu ao Brasil parte da cota de carne para China; efeito seria limitado em 2026
item.description: O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva afirmou nesta segunda-feira que o Uruguai cedeu ao Brasil parte da cota de exportação de carne bovina do país para a China, uma vez que os frigoríficos brasileiros já completaram a cota nacional de embarques em 2026 ao país asiático.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva afirmou nesta segunda-feira que o Uruguai cedeu ao Brasil parte da cota de exportação de carne bovina do país para a China, uma vez que os frigoríficos brasileiros já completaram a cota nacional de embarques em 2026 ao país asiático. "Agradeci a autorização concedida ao Brasil para uso do excedente da cota uruguaia de exportação de carne bovina para a China", disse Lula, em uma publicação no X. O Ministério de Relações Exteriores do Uruguai não comentou o assunto imediatamente. A postagem de Lula no X foi feita após um encontro bilateral com o presidente do Uruguai, Yamandú Orsi, em Nova York, no contexto da Assembleia Geral da ONU que ocorre nesta semana. "Tratamos de temas da agenda bilateral, em especial infraestrutura e comércio agrícola", acrescentou Lula. A associação de empresas do setor de carnes Abiec afirmou que "avalia como positiva toda iniciativa que possa ampliar o acesso da carne bovina brasileira ao mercado chinês". "Neste momento, porém, um eventual aproveitamento do excedente da cota uruguaia teria efeito limitado em 2026, considerando o tempo necessário para negociação, embarque e trânsito da mercadoria até a China", afirmou a Abiec em nota. Enquanto o Brasil já completou sua cota com tarifa mais baixa de 1,1 milhão de toneladas para 2026, o Uruguai ainda teria volumes disponíveis para este ano. Os volumes, no entanto, não estão claros e a negociação ainda precisaria de um aval da China, que passou a taxar em 55% os volumes extracota. Conforme notou a Abiec, já em novembro o Brasil começa a embarcar produto para a China para completar sua própria cota de 2027, o que tornaria limitada a utilização do remanescente da cota uruguaia de 2026 pelos frigoríficos brasileiros. "Para 2027, a medida pode representar uma alternativa importante, especialmente diante da cota brasileira de 1,128 milhão de toneladas e do risco de seu esgotamento já nos primeiros meses do ano, caso se mantenha o atual ritmo de vendas", acrescentou a Abiec. Uma antecipação de embarques de carne bovina do Brasil para a China, para o cumprimento da cota de 2027, pode levar ao [USN:L1N4590LY TEXT:"preenchimento"] rápido dos volumes totais de 1,128 milhão de toneladas estabelecidos para o ano, avaliou o presidente da Abiec, Roberto Perosa, na semana passada. Por isso, a Abiec reiterou que defende previsibilidade e mecanismos que permitam distribuir melhor os embarques ao longo do ano, "preservando o fluxo comercial com o principal destino da carne bovina brasileira".

item.title: Newsom signs bill limiting investor influence in California law firms
item.description: California, one of the largest US legal markets, has joined Colorado and Illinois in enacting legislation to limit investor influence in law firms amid surging interest in deals that allow outside capital to fuel lawyers' business.
item.dc:creator: David Thomas
item.content:encoded: California, one of the largest US legal markets, has joined Colorado and [USN:L6N4470UV TEXT:"Illinois"] in enacting legislation to limit investor influence in law firms amid surging interest in deals that allow outside capital to fuel lawyers' business. California Governor Gavin Newsom on Sunday signed legislation prohibiting business entities from interfering or attempting to "influence the professional judgment of a licensed attorney or litigant regarding any substantive litigation decision," including lawyers' settlement decisions and what cases and clients they take. Violators, including attorney recipients of outside capital, face statutory damages of $10,000 per violation, or three times the damages suffered by a client. California Assembly member Ash Kalra, who authored AB 2305, did not immediately respond to a request for comment. In a statement last month, Kalra said, "The principle is simple: when you hire a lawyer, the person making decisions about your case should be your lawyer — not a private equity entity looking for profit." Consumer Attorneys of California, a trade group that backed the legislation, said in a statement Monday that the state is "setting the standard for the rest of the country to follow." Investors and other non-lawyers are broadly prohibited in the United States from owning direct stakes in law firms or sharing in attorney fees. However, a growing number of firms are inking deals to spin off their non-legal, back-office operations like human resources or marketing into a separate organization called a management services organization (MSO), that is owned or partly owned by outside investors. Such deals can provide an influx of capital for a law firm, which pays the MSO from its revenues but does not share fees. Some MSOs serve multiple firms. California's new law applies to business entities that raise or manage capital and are involved in litigation practice "no matter how it is legally structured, labeled, organized, or operated." Trisha Rich, a partner at Holland & Knight whose team has closed more than 30 legal industry MSO deals this year, told Reuters the California law does not "change a single thing," since existing attorney professional rules already guard against outside influence on legal decision-making. She said the similar laws in Illinois and Colorado had not affected MSO deal-making in those states, and that there had been no enforcement efforts tied to the provisions. Newsom last year [USN:L2N3VV010 TEXT:"signed into law a bill"] that prohibited attorneys in the state from splitting fees with out-of-state "alternative business structures," unless there is a contract stating that the fees will be shared, as well as other conditions.

item.title: Mercados financieros de Argentina operan mixtos, comitiva FMI visita el país para revisión programa
item.description: La plaza financiera argentina cerró mayormente mixta el lunes, con una marcada reducción de negocios, en momentos en que los inversores centran su atención en la visita de una misión del Fondo Monetario Internacional (FMI) para la tercera revisión del programa de 20.000 millones de dólares con el país.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
